name: 66 GERMAN
description: 66 German (Sechsundsechzig): two-player trick-taking. 24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9). 6 cards each; turned card for trump. First to 66 trick points (and declare) wins the hand. Marriages (K+Q same suit) 20 or 40; close stock to force follow suit. Game to 7 match points.

content.text: 66 German (Sechsundsechzig): two-player trick-taking. 24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9). 6 cards each; turned card for trump. First to 66 trick points (and declare) wins the hand. Marriages (K+Q same suit) 20 or 40; close stock to force follow suit. Game to 7 match points.
German two-player game (Sechsundsechzig); said to originate around 1652 in Paderborn. Related to Schnapsen (Austria).

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 2
Optimal Players: 2
Partnerships: None (two-player duel)

Type: Standard 24-card pack made by removing 2–8 from a French- or German-suited deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9 in each of four suits).
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9 in four suits)
Score markers or sevens/eights for game points
Table space

Cards per Player: 6
Dealing Pattern: Dealer shuffles and deals 6 cards to each player (in packets or singly), then turns the next card face up to set the trump suit and places the remaining 11 cards crosswise on top as the stock (talon).

items.text: Three-player 66: Three-handed game in which all 24 cards are dealt out, eight to each player. One player chooses trumps from an initial three-card packet, there is no talon, players must follow suit and try to win tricks, and marriages still score 20 or 40 while the aim remains to reach 66 card points.

Four-player partnership 66: Partnership variant where two teams of two play with a 24-card pack and aim for 66 points as a side. Sources describe adjusted dealing, trump selection, and partnership scoring but retain the same marriage and trick-point structure as the base game.
